Subject: Insurance requirements for MSA — addl insured + cyber waiver

Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning. A couple quick asks from procurement/legal at HeliosCloud as we review the draft MSA and order form:

- We need Redwood to accept Additional Insured naming for our parent entity (HeliosCloud, Inc.) on the general liability endorsement.
- Our security team is asking for confirmation a carrier will provide a waiver of subrogation on the cyber policy or a written insurer-side waiver for our mutual indemnity carve-outs.
- Finally, please confirm the expected COI delivery cadence and whether endorsements (CG 20 10 / CG 20 26 equivalents) can be provided prior to Go-Live.

I'll attach the procurement worksheet; Sasha (our broker) is on copy and can coordinate proof of coverage. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Tom

Subject: Re: Insurance requirements for MSA — addl insured + cyber waiver

Tom — thanks, got it. Looping in Aditya (legal) and Kim (account lead) to confirm how far we can go on the endorsements and subrogation waiver. Quick notes:

- Additional Insured: we typically add customers as Additional Insured on the commercial GL policy via endorsement; legal will confirm exact wording we can accept.
- Cyber Waiver: this is trickier — our cyber insurer is often unwilling to provide broad waivers of subrogation. We can request an insurer-side waiver specific to this contract, but it may require an underwriter review and could be carrier-dependent.
- COI cadence: we can share a COI prior to Go-Live and follow up with final endorsements within 30 days of execution in most cases; I'll confirm firm timing.

Aditya/Kim — can you please advise on: (1) acceptable Additional Insured language (we prefer a limited endorsement vs. blanket), (2) whether we can commit to pursuing an insurer-side waiver for cyber, and (3) whether a 30-day post-execution endorsement delivery is acceptable here?

Thanks — I'll hold on scheduling a call until I hear back.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Insurance requirements for MSA — addl insured + cyber waiver

Marissa / Kim —

I reviewed the redlines and sketched a practical position for negotiation:

1) Additional Insured: we can agree to name "HeliosCloud, Inc." and its subsidiaries as Additional Insured but only via a CG 20 26 or equivalent that is limited to liability arising out of our operations under the MSA. We should avoid blanket broad-form AI language. Proposed clause: "Redwood Inference shall procure, at its expense, an endorsement naming HeliosCloud, Inc. as Additional Insured, limited to liability arising out of Redwood's services under this Agreement."

2) Waiver of Subrogation (Cyber): our cyber carrier historically declines insurer-side waivers for third-party contracts except in limited cases. We can commit to (a) requesting an insurer-side waiver; (b) if denied, Redwood will not assert subrogation against HeliosCloud arising from a claim covered by Redwood's cyber policy (i.e., contractual waiver) to mirror the practical effect. That hybrid approach usually satisfies counterparties and avoids forcing carrier acceptance.

3) COI / Endorsement timing: commit to providing a COI at execution and commercially reasonable efforts to deliver the requested endorsements within 30 days. If Helios needs endorsements earlier, we can ask our broker to escalate but cannot guarantee carrier turnaround time.

I attached redline language in the shared drive (MSA_redlines_20290313.docx). Kim/David, weigh in on commercial risk appetite and whether underwriting delay is a blocker for Go-Live.

Thanks,
Aditya
Associate GC — Redwood Inference
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@brooklinebrokerage.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 10:22:00 -04:00

Marissa/Tom — Sasha here (Helios' broker). Quick context from the market: carriers will consider an insurer-side cyber waiver only when the policyholder (Redwood) can demonstrate specific controls and limits. If Redwood is willing to provide a contractual waiver of subrogation as fallback and to order endorsement issuance within 30 days post-signature, most buyers will accept that.

I'll attach a sample endorsement wording that Helios' legal prefers. If Redwood can sign the limited AI endorsement + contractual waiver fallback, I can route the request to the underwriter and push for expedited handling.

Regards,
Sasha
Brookline Brokerage

Tom — following up with the team and next steps:

- Additional Insured: Redwood can provide a limited Additional Insured endorsement naming "HeliosCloud, Inc." and its subsidiaries. The endorsement will be limited to liability arising from Redwood's services under the MSA (we avoid broad-form AI wording).
- Cyber Waiver: Redwood will request an insurer-side waiver from our cyber carrier. If the carrier declines, Redwood will include a contractual waiver of subrogation in the MSA so Helios receives the practical protection.
- COI and timing: Redwood will provide a COI at execution and use commercially reasonable efforts to furnish the requested endorsements within 30 days. Sasha, please escalate to the underwriter once you have Redwood's formal request.

Attached: MSA_redlines_20290313.docx (contains the proposed language for AI and the contractual waiver fallback). Please confirm if Helios can accept the limited AI + contractual fallback and 30-day endorsement delivery. If you need endorsement before Go-Live, say so and we'll coordinate.
